name: Connecticut
sources: CT DRS, 2025 Form CT-1040 Tax Calculation Schedule (portal.ct.gov/-/media/drs/forms/2025/income/ct-1040-tcs_1225.pdf): Table A personal exemptions $15,000 / $24,000 / $12,000 / $19,000 less $1,000 per $1,000 of CT AGI over $30,000 / $48,000 / $24,000 / $38,000; Table B rates 2%-6.99%; Table C 2% rate phase-out add-back; Table D recapture; Table E personal tax credit decimals

CT DRS, 2025 Form CT-1040 instructions (portal.ct.gov/-/media/drs/forms/2025/income/2025-ct-1040-instructions_1225.pdf): Tax Calculation Schedule lines 1-10, CT AGI less exemption, tax = (B + C + D) x (1 - Table E decimal)

CT DRS, 2025 and 2026 State Tax Developments, income tax (portal.ct.gov/drs/miscellaneous-taxes/other-tax-page/state-tax-developments): no change to rates, brackets, exemptions, phase-out, recapture or personal credit for 2026
provisional: All rates, the personal exemption, the 2% phase-out add-back, the recapture and the personal tax credit are the 2025 tables; Connecticut does not index them and no 2026 change was enacted, but the 2026 schedule is not yet published
notes: The 2% rate phase-out and the benefit recapture are built into the brackets, so rates above about $56,500 (single) / $100,500 (joint) are effective rates and rise smoothly rather than in $25-$180 steps (within about $180 of the real tables).

The personal exemption is shown as the standard deduction, and the personal tax credit (1%-75% of tax at lower incomes) is approximated as $150 per filer, so results below about $64,500 single / $100,500 joint can be off by up to about $120 (single) or $250 (joint).
The property tax credit (up to $300) and the pension, IRA and Social Security subtractions are not included.
